title: Peer-proximity shard placement and soft-fallback design
content:
Summary:

This document proposes a lightweight, latency-first shard placement strategy that prioritizes GPU peer proximity, link quality, and workload affinity, combined with a ‘soft-fallback’ mechanism when collective performance degrades. The goal is to reduce per-request tail latency and NCCL retransmit/stripe stalls for typical inference workloads (short sequences, bursty QPS) without forcing global re-shards on transient network noise.

Context and motivation:
- We run multi-GPU inference across heterogeneous racks and instance types. Network topology (within-node NVLink, intra-rack RDMA, inter-rack fabric) produces widely varying collective latencies.
- Existing placement heuristics optimize for uniform bandwidth or capacity; they often ignore transient link congestion and kernel-level contention patterns.
- Recent incidents show spikes in NCCL all-reduce latency correlate with suboptimal peer mappings and mismatched chunk sizes.

Design goals:
1) Keep common-case latency low: prefer mappings with minimal hop count and highest steady-state bandwidth for the dominant collective patterns (all-reduce/all-gather for KV syncs and activation slicing).
2) Avoid global re-shard churn: prefer ephemeral local fallbacks over full reconfiguration when degradations are short-lived.
3) Be conservative about expensive operations: re-sharding or migrating large KV partitions is heavy—must be rare and observable.
4) Expose simple knobs for ops: admission thresholds, hedging aggressiveness, and probe duration.

Key ideas (high level):
- Peer proximity score: compute a small, continuously-updated score for every candidate placement based on topology (same GPU board / same host / same rack), measured one-way latency, and packet drop/retry counters.
- Affinity term: incorporate model-stage affinity (tensor-parallel neighbors, pipeline stage locality) so KV shards that are hot for certain layers prefer co-location.
- Soft-fallback: when a placement’s score falls below a threshold, begin a staged mitigation: 1) local NCCL tuning (switch chunk size / algorithm), 2) hedged RPCs to an alternative compatible placement, 3) selective request replication for critical tails, 4) if sustained, schedule an asynchronous re-shard.
- Adaptive chunking: dynamically pick NCCL chunk sizes per-collective based on bandwidth*latency profile and activation size distribution. Prefer smaller chunks on lossy/variable links to reduce head-of-line stalls.

Placement algorithm (sketch):
1) Gather inputs: topology matrix (static), recent metrics (latency histograms, retransmit counts per link, per-collective completion times), resource fitness (free GPU memory, KV partition size).
2) Candidate generation: for a requested shard set, enumerate candidate node sets constrained by placement policies (tenant isolation, reserved capacity). For each candidate, compute score = w1*proximity + w2*bandwidth_est + w3*affinity - w4*load_penalty.
3) Quick accept: if a candidate’s score is > high_threshold and passes capacity checks, place immediately.
4) Probation placement: if best candidate is borderline, place but enable soft-fallback probes (see below).
5) Deferred re-shard: only triggered when fallback probes show sustained >X% latency degredation over T minutes or retransmit rate >Y.

NCCL and kernel tuning knobs we recommend exposing: 
- chunk_size_bytes: per-collective initial chunk size (default 1MB for stable RDMA, 256KB for volatile links).
- algorithm_hint: prefer ring/tree/auto depending on peer count and link symmetry.
- num_chunks_in_flight: controls pipelining depth for large collectives.
- ib_timeout/rc_retries: tune conservative values on racks with known lossy links.
- sync_barrier_timeout: small timeout for early detection of hung collectives and trigger fallback.
Notes: in testing, moving from a 1MB to 256KB chunk for asymmetric cross-rack collectives reduced 99th by ~25% at modest throughput levels.

KV streaming and shard layout rules:
- Streamed KV transfers: when warming or re-sharding large KV partitions, stream in prioritized order: hot prefixes (recently-accessed keys), then layer-wise activation slices, then cold tails. This reduces cache miss pain during phased migration.
- Sub-shard fragmentation: allow large logical shards to be split into sub-shards with local proxies (helps smaller migration units). Sub-shard size defaults to 128MB but should be configurable.
- Read-path fast-path: keep local caches of frequently used KV prefixes and ensure placement score weights prefer nodes that already hold a hot cache copy.

Soft-fallback state machine (per-request/collective):
- INIT: normal execution with primary placement. Collect metrics.
- PROBE: upon detecting slow collective (completion > baseline*T), run local NCCL tuning (adjust chunk size and pipelining). If no improvement within N attempts, open hedged RPC to secondary placement.
- HEDGE_ACTIVE: duplicate read-only requests to secondary placement for tail reduction; only commit results from the first responder. Log cost delta.
- MIGRATE_PENDING: if degradation persists (sustained over window), mark shard for asynchronous migration to higher-scoring placement during low load.
- ROLLBACK: if migration causes regressions or instability, rollback to old placement and raise incident.

Signals and thresholds (suggested defaults):
- baseline multiplier T = 2.0 (i.e., if collective takes >2x baseline median), trigger PROBE.
- probe attempts N = 2 before hedging.
- sustained window for migrate = 10 minutes with >30% requests degraded.
- hedging rate cap = 5% of traffic to limit cost.

Metrics to capture and expose in Console:
- collective_completion_ms by placement and collective_type (p50/p95/p99)
- retransmit_rate per link / per host
- hedged_request_pct and hedged_latency_reduction (absolute ms and % tail drop)
- migration_count and average time-to-migrate per GB
- cost_delta_of_hedging (tokens/time-per-GB-equivalent)

Experiment plan / validation steps:
1) Simulation (offline): feed historical placement + link metrics into a placement-simulator to compute expected p99 improvements and migration churn. Parameter sweep for weights w1..w4 and thresholds.
2) Canary in Dedicated pool: pick a small tenant group; run placement scorer and enable PROBE/HEDGE for a subset of shards (non-critical). Measure p99 and hedging cost.
3) Microbench: run synthetic collectives with controlled packet loss/latency to validate chunk-size heuristics and NCCL algorithm switching.
4) End-to-end: measure real-app p99 (chat/qa traffic), track incidents pre/post rollout.

Rollout and operational playbook:
- Phase 0: feature flags behind tenant opt-in + telemetry only.
- Phase 1: enable scoring + probe for read-heavy KV shards in Dedicated region A. Monitor for 48h.
- Phase 2: widen hedging to 2% traffic, enable automated async migrate for shards with sustained degradation.
- Phase 3: open to wider fleet, expose placement insights in Console.
- Safety kills: global flag to disable hedging and migration; automatic disable on repeated migration rollbacks >3 in 24h.

Open questions / decision points:
- Weighting: how do we pick w1..w4? Start with topology-heavy weights and tune by simulation?
- Probe cost: hedging reduces tail but adds cost—what guardrails for cost attribution to customer vs internal optimization?
- Consistency: do hedged reads require strict KV versioning or is best-effort ok for inference? (Prefer best-effort if results are deterministic and side-effect free.)
- Interaction with autoscaler: aggressive placement/migration could interact poorly with autoscale-driven instance churn. Need tests.

Appendix: quick sim notes (local perf test, Nov 2024)
- Setup: 4-node rack with mixed NVLink+RDMA; synthetic activation sizes 8KB-64KB; baseline chunk=1MB.
- Observation: asymmetric cross-rack links had 40–70ms spikes at p99 due to single large chunk stalls; switching to 256KB and increasing in-flight chunks from 2->6 reduced p99 by ~27% but raised median by 1–2ms due to additional scheduling overhead.
- Hedging: hedging 3% of read-paths reduced observed p99 by additional 10% on bursts; cost measured as ~+2% CPU and +1.8% bandwidth in tests.

TODOs and next actions:
- [ ] Build placement-simulator and run parameter sweeps for weights and thresholds (owner: Diego).
- [ ] Implement pivotable NCCL config layer to change chunk_size and algorithm at runtime (owner: Owen).
- [ ] Create Console telemetry dashboard for hedging_cost and collective_completion by placement (owner: Kara).
- [ ] Draft tenant-facing note explaining hedged requests and potential small cost increases (owner: Priya).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative on migration frequency; the soft-fallback path is meant to catch transient network issues without global churn.
- Implementation should prioritize observability hooks: every probe/hedge/migration must be logged with causality metadata for post-mortem.

End of doc.
